title: Give the row-level data-scope policy a real tenant dimension on both the read and the write path
goal: system_role_data_scope already has a tenant_id column and a (tenant_id, role_key) unique key, yet five of the six code points that touch it work on role_key alone: the middleware struct has no TenantID field, loadRoleDataScopePolicies filters by role_key only, resolveDataScopeMode returns all when any matching row is all, UpdateDataScopePolicy never assigns TenantID and conflicts on role_key, ListDataScopePolicies reads system_role with no tenant predicate, ensureRoleKeyExists accepts a key that exists in any tenant, and RoleService.loadRoleDataScopes echoes whichever row was scanned last. Measured effect: tenant A's console lists 53 roles while owning 3, A writes a policy for a role that exists only in B, and setting the shared key to all raised B's ordinary user from 1 visible row to 3 (and the reverse direction behaved identically). This wave closes the tenant dimension on both sides, backfills historical tenant_id = 0 rows where the owner is unambiguous, and validates that custom deptIds belong to the calling tenant.
findings: F7 (P0): ListDataScopePolicies queries system_role with only deleted_at IS NULL, so the data-scope console lists every tenant's roles.
F8 (P0): ensureRoleKeyExists checks existence in any tenant, so tenant A successfully wrote a data-scope policy for a role that exists only in tenant B (code 200).
F9 (P1): UpdateDataScopePolicy builds the policy without TenantID and declares OnConflict on role_key alone, producing tenant_id = 0 rows that apply to every tenant.

F10 (P0): SystemRoleDataScope has no TenantID field and resolveDataScopeMode widens to all if any matching row is all, so one tenant's write changes another tenant's effective visible rows (1 -> 3 measured in both directions).
F11 (P1): custom deptIds are stored verbatim with no tenant ownership check; tenant A submitted tenant B's department 203 and it was persisted.
F13 (P1): RoleService.loadRoleDataScopes filters by role_key only, so a tenant's role list echoes another tenant's or the global row's dataScope.

out: Changing the five data-scope modes or their resolution priority among themselves
Changing the tenant_admin / tenant_member exemption from row-level policy

implementationNotes: Thread the tenant through explicitly rather than reading it inside helpers: DataScopeMiddleware already resolves tenant.FromGin(c), so pass that TenantID into applyRoleDataScopePolicy and loadRoleDataScopePolicies instead of adding a hidden dependency.
Keep fail-closed intact. rolePoliciesCoverAll must still deny when a role has no row for the resolved tenant; adding the predicate must not turn a missing row into a pass-through.
PermissionService has no tenantOwnerID equivalent today; mirror RoleService.tenantOwnerID() rather than duplicating tenant resolution logic.
resolvePolicySubject already accepts a tenantId and is correct; the defect is ensureRoleKeyExists and UpdateDataScopePolicy. Fix the validation, not the subject mapping.

The migration copies, never moves: it reads only the tenant_id = 0 row (the pre-fix effective policy every tenant saw) and inserts a per-owner copy, leaving the platform row in place because the platform scope still reads it. A policy that exists only under another tenant is deliberately not copied — that row is another tenant's authority and copying it would freeze F10 into the data. Duplicated role_keys are therefore replicated to each owner rather than left global; the duplicated set is listed in the evidence SQL snapshot so an operator can review it.
Do not invent a policy for a role that owns none anywhere. The runtime fails closed on a missing row, and backfilling `all` would silently widen a role nobody ever configured.

Guard the backfill on information_schema, exactly like 000024: a database can record version 24 while 000024's DDL never ran, and on such a database tenant_id does not exist yet. Unguarded, the INSERT turns startup into a failure loop; guarded, it degrades to a no-op and 000024's repair does the work on the next real upgrade.
Validate deptIds against system_dept under the resolved tenant before persisting, and reject the whole request rather than silently dropping foreign IDs.

boundaryCrossings: platform (tenant context) <-> system/iam (policy rows) <-> system/org (dept ownership)
riskNodes: DataScopeMiddleware (hot path for every governed request)
loadRoleDataScopes (console echo used by operators to judge policy state)
graphFocus: every SQL touching system_role_data_scope and system_role inside the data-scope console

commands: cd backend && gofmt -l internal/ modules/ pkg/
runtimeEvidence: L3 before/after: tenant B's user row count stays constant when tenant A changes the shared role_key policy
L2: data-scope console total equals the calling tenant's own role count; PUT for a foreign role_key is rejected
SQL snapshot: no new row with tenant_id = 0 after an operator saves a policy
migration re-run is a no-op and down leaves data intact

humanGates: Approve the backfill policy: the tenant_id = 0 row is copied (not moved) onto every tenant that owns the role key, because it was the policy every one of those tenants was already governed by; nothing is copied from one tenant onto another.
Confirm that platform-scope callers (tenant_id = 0 subject) keep seeing the full policy list, since the console is also used by the platform administrator.
completionChecklist: SystemRoleDataScope carries TenantID and every read path filters on it
UpdateDataScopePolicy assigns TenantID and conflicts on (tenant_id, role_key)
ListDataScopePolicies, ensureRoleKeyExists and loadRoleDataScopes all carry tenant predicates
custom deptIds rejected when they do not belong to the resolved tenant
No new tenant_id = 0 row produced by any console action
